title: Federal Rule 56 — summary judgment
summary: Summary judgment decides a claim or defense without trial when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It examines an evidentiary record rather than only a complaint.

sections.Role in the course: Summary judgment decides a claim or defense without trial when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It examines an evidentiary record rather than only a complaint.
sections.What to examine: Identify the material elements under substantive law, who bears the trial burden, the movant’s supported showing, and the response. Ask whether a reasonable factfinder could rule for the nonmovant under the applicable evidentiary standard, drawing reasonable inferences in that party’s favor.
